newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa at new 4-mth low, 968 support breached.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa at new 4-mth low, 968 support breached.

text.p: Cocoa futures dived to a new four-month low on Thursday on speculative long liquidation as the market resumed its downward spiral after taking a brief pause on Wednesday.
September, London's benchmark, was driven to the session's floor at 965 stg per tonne, the lowest level since March 10, after breaching Tuesday's low and key support at 968.
It eventually finished midday at 966 stg, a steep 20 stg down on the day. Most-active December shed 14 stg at 1,003 after ranging between 1,003 and 1,014. The market was called five stg down.
"It was spec selling but conditions were thin," said a trader.
Volume totalled just 3,768 lots, mainly outright trading.
Traders said London's next move would hinge on how New York would do this afternoon. September could find a new support at just above 950 stg.
The U.S. cocoa market was called $15-$20 lower.
A break below $1,525-$1,520 per tonne on December in New York could set the market back below the major uptrend line established since last February.
"It will be quite bearish and it will spark big spec long liquidation," said one trader.
LIFFE cocoa's downturn had a brief respite on Wednesday after five trading days of decline. Yesterday's session was overshadowed by sterling/mark volatility which also sidelined many industry buyers.

Broker GNI said Wednesday's news on trade expectation of higher Ivorian cocoa farmgate prices for next season could be viewed as short-term positive factor as it would encourage holding over a larger portion of the mid-crop to mix with the new season's main-crop beans.
